candidates.attacker_control: The XML document itself (input to XmlMapper.readValue / XmlFactory.createParser for InputStream, Reader, char[] and byte[] sources) is fully attacker-controlled and is handed unchanged to _xmlInputFactory.createXMLStreamReader(...). For the readResolve path, the factory class name and serialized object graph are attacker-influenced if the application JDK-deserializes an XmlFactory/XmlMapper from untrusted data.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: XmlFactory.java:112-116 does contain the [dataformat-xml#190] mitigation (IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=FALSE) and the default XmlMapper path reaches it, so classic external-entity XXE is blocked for the self-created default factory; standard providers (Woodstox, JDK SJSXP) map this property to external entity/DTD resolution. XML with a DOCTYPE is intentionally supported (FormatDetectionTest.testSimpleValidDoctype; XmlFactory.hasXMLFormat handles '<!DOCTYPE'), so DTD acceptance is a deliberate compatibility choice. Grep confirms no SUPPORT_DTD / IS_REPLACING_ENTITY_REFERENCES setting anywhere, confirming the residual gap. The readResolve issue requires the application to JDK-deserialize untrusted bytes, an already dangerous pattern, so it is a hardening regression rather than an independent primitive. Other sinks inspected and found non-exploitable from source: ToXmlGenerator output escaping/writeRaw, XmlBeanSerializerBase/_orderAttributesFirst array handling, XmlTypeResolverBuilder type-id encode/decode, XmlSerializerProvider, JacksonXmlAnnotationIntrospector, JAXB introspectors, WrapperHandlingDeserializer/XmlTextDeserializer.
candidates.impact: Resource-exhaustion denial of service while parsing a small malicious document that declares recursively expanding internal entities (consequence of leaving DTD support enabled), and, on paths where external entity support is not effectively disabled (caller-supplied factory, readResolve-restored factory, or a StAX implementation ignoring the property), XML External Entity processing that can disclose local files or cause outbound requests (SSRF) from the parsing host. The readResolve path also loads/instantiates a stream-controlled class name and silently downgrades the factory's security settings, so a previously hardened mapper can be restored unprotected.
candidates.prerequisites: Application parses untrusted XML with default XmlMapper/XmlFactory (no code change needed): DTD processing and internal entity expansion are exposed. For stronger XXE impact, the effective XMLInputFactory must not have external entities disabled, i.e. the application supplies its own XMLInputFactory, or the factory was restored through readResolve/JDK deserialization, or the deployed StAX implementation does not honor javax.xml.stream.isSupportingExternalEntities (woodstox-core 5.0.2 is test-scope in pom.xml, so the production StAX provider is deployer-chosen).
candidates.root_cause: In the protected XmlFactory constructor (XmlFactory.java:104-123) the XMLInputFactory is hardened only inside `if (xmlIn == null)`: it sets IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false but never sets XMLInputFactory.SUPPORT_DTD=false, so the default XmlMapper still lets the StAX layer parse DOCTYPE declarations and the internal DTD subset and expand internal entity references. The same guard means no hardening is applied when an XMLInputFactory is passed in by the application (constructors at XmlFactory.java:90-102, mirrored by XmlMapper(XMLInputFactory) / XmlMapper(XMLInputFactory,XMLOutputFactory) at XmlMapper.java:55-64), and when JDK deserialization rebuilds the factory: readResolve (XmlFactory.java:184-204) instantiates factory classes named by the serialized stream via Class.forName(...).newInstance() and passes them as non-null xmlIn to the same constructor, so a deserialized XmlFactory/XmlMapper silently loses the external-entity hardening.
candidates.title: XmlFactory leaves DTD/entity processing enabled and applies external-entity hardening only to self-created XMLInputFactory instances (skipped for caller-supplied and readResolve-restored factories)
candidates.trace: XmlMapper() -> new XmlFactory() -> protected ctor: xmlIn == null -> XMLInputFactory.newInstance() + IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES=false (no SUPPORT_DTD=false, no IS_REPLACING_ENTITY_REFERENCES=false) -> _initFactories -> _xmlInputFactory retained. Parser creation (_createParser for InputStream/Reader/char[]/byte[], XmlFactory.java:533-606) calls _xmlInputFactory.createXMLStreamReader(input); _initializeXmlReader (647-654) only advances to the first START_ELEMENT, so DOCTYPE/internal-subset processing happens inside the StAX provider before Jackson sees any token, and declared entities are expanded into text collected by XmlTokenStream. Secondary path: readObject (210-216) reads _jdkXmlInFactory/_jdkXmlOutFactory strings; readResolve (185-204) does Class.forName(...).newInstance() for both and calls the constructor with non-null factories, bypassing the line-112 hardening branch so the rebuilt mapper parses with default factory settings.
candidates.unverified: No code was executed: entity-expansion/DoS behavior and whether the deployed StAX implementation honors IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES (and what entity/expansion limits it enforces) are unverified. The production StAX provider is unknown because woodstox-core is test-scope. The upstream fix/commit corresponding to this benchmark case could not be independently verified, and the snapshot already contains the dataformat-xml#190 mitigation, so this candidate describes a residual hardening gap rather than a demonstrated exploit. No runtime confirmation is claimed.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611 Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (with CWE-776 / CWE-400 entity-expansion denial-of-service component)

coverage_summary: All 33 main-source files under src/main/java (annotation, deser, ser, util, jaxb, root packages) were read or searched; 102 of 103 repository files are model-visible (1 file excluded by the sensitive-name/path filter, not inspected). The P1 relation index covers 99 Java files / 1619 symbols but only 18 files were syntax-parsed and it explicitly provides no control-flow, data-flow, semantic resolution, Spring enforcement, or reachability evidence (2396 unresolved calls), so index edges were used only for navigation and every reported location was verified against source text. Test sources were skimmed for security-relevant expectations; pom.xml and .travis.yml were reviewed for dependency/build assumptions. No code, tests, or scanners were executed and no external services were contacted.
limitations: No runtime verification: entity-expansion behavior, DTD handling and StAX-provider property support (Woodstox 5.0.2 vs JDK SJSXP) cannot be confirmed from source alone; woodstox-core is test-scoped in pom.xml, so production parser behavior is deployment-dependent.

The benchmark's ground-truth vulnerability/fix for this case could not be independently identified; the snapshot already contains the dataformat-xml#190 external-entity mitigation, so this candidate is a residual-hardening lead rather than a demonstrated exploit.

One repository file is excluded from view by the sensitive-name/path filter and was not reviewed; binary-like files are skipped and the relation index parsed only a subset of Java files, with no data-flow or control-flow analysis.

No comparison against the upstream fixed revision, patch, CVE metadata, or previous runs was performed (prohibited), so the reported weakness type and impact classification are source-based inferences.

rejected_leads.lead: XmlFactory.readResolve() loads and instantiates classes named by the serialized stream via Class.forName(_jdkXmlInFactory).newInstance() (XmlFactory.java:193-194).
rejected_leads.reason: Attacker must already control JDK-serialized object bytes deserialized by the victim application (a precondition that itself implies serious exposure), and the cast constrains usable classes to XMLInputFactory implementations. Kept as part of the submitted candidate's hardening-bypass trace rather than a separate finding; no independently reachable attacker-controlled input path was evidenced in this repository.

rejected_leads.lead: XmlFactory._initializeXmlReader loops `while (sr.next() != START_ELEMENT);` (XmlFactory.java:647-654), which can surface a raw NoSuchElementException/RuntimeException instead of a clean JsonParseException for input without a root element; XmlTokenStream._skipUntilTag can throw IllegalStateException (XmlTokenStream.java:387).
rejected_leads.reason: Robustness/error-reporting defects on malformed input; the StAX reader terminates (no unbounded loop demonstrated) and no memory-safety or resource-amplification impact was established from source alone.

rejected_leads.lead: FromXmlParser numeric accessors are unimplemented stubs returning null/0 (FromXmlParser.java:861-907), and some streaming paths desynchronize logical vs. underlying reader state (FromXmlParser.getValueAsString / XmlTokenStream.convertToString).
rejected_leads.reason: Correctness/streaming-API issues; these values are not used as security decisions by data binding in this version and no attacker-controlled privilege boundary was identified.

rejected_leads.lead: Caller-supplied XMLInputFactory is not hardened by XmlFactory/XmlMapper (XmlFactory.java:90-102, XmlMapper.java:55-64).
rejected_leads.reason: This is the configuration footgun that forms part of the submitted candidate's root cause (conditional hardening), so it is not split out as a second candidate.

summary: Reviewed the jackson-dataformat-xml snapshot (2.7.8-SNAPSHOT; 102 model-visible files: 33 main sources, ~66 tests, pom/README/travis). The strongest source-evidenced weakness is XmlFactory's StAX parser hardening: external-entity expansion is disabled only when XmlFactory itself creates the XMLInputFactory, and DTD support is never disabled. XmlMapper default construction and all parser factory methods route through this configuration, so untrusted XML still triggers DOCTYPE/internal-DTD/entity handling (entity-expansion resource exhaustion), and the hardening is silently skipped when a caller supplies an XMLInputFactory or when JDK deserialization rebuilds it via readResolve, re-opening XXE-style exposure on those paths. No command injection, path traversal, or unsafe bean-mapping logic was found in the module; other leads are recorded as rejected. The snapshot already contains the historic [dataformat-xml#190] mitigation, so the candidate is submitted as a lead, not a confirmed exploit.
